question.worked_solution:
First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-7}+\frac{B}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-7)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-7)^{3}$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-9x+16=A(x-7)^{2}+B(x-7)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=7,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(7)^{2}-9(7)+16 & =A(7-7)^{2}+B(7-7)+C \\ 2 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=6$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(6)^{2}-9(6)+16 & =A(6-7)^{2}+B(6-7)+C \\ -2 & =A-B+2 \\ A-B & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=8$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(8)^{2}-9(8)+16 & =A(8-7)^{2}+B(8-7)+C \\ 8 & =A+B+2 \\ A+B & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=-4$ and $A+B=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =-4+6 \\ A & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1+B & =6 \\ B & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}=\frac{1}{x-7}+\frac{5}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-7)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-7}+\frac{5}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-7)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-7}\,\text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{(x-7)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{(x-7)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-7|-\frac{5}{x-7}-\frac{1}{(x-7)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
